For Caramelized Onion Financier: Finely dice onion and garlic. Sauté in 10g butter over low heat until deeply caramelized and sweet, about 25-30 minutes. Cool. Melt remaining 60g butter until browned (beurre noisette). Strain solids. Whisk egg whites, almond flour, granulated sugar, and all-purpose flour in a bowl. Fold in cooled caramelized onion-garlic mixture and browned butter. Pour batter into mini financier molds. Bake at 170°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and cooked through. Cool completely.

For Crispy Potato Tuiles: Peel potato. Slice paper-thin using a mandoline. Place slices on parchment-lined baking sheet. Lightly brush with melted butter. Season with a pinch of salt. Bake at 160°C until golden and crisp, about 10-15 minutes. Watch closely to prevent burning. Cool on a wire rack.

Assembly: Arrange 6-9 financiers on an elegant serving platter. Gently unmold the set crémeux. Place a small piece or sphere of crémeux atop each financier. Carefully place a crispy potato tuile artistically on each petit four, standing upright or angled. Use a dropper or small spoon to place a tiny droplet or a thin brushstroke of the warm chicken essence gel beside or on a part of each petit four. Garnish with a few micro herbs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Rice Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A small cluster of three to four golden brown fritters rests on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The fritters are irregularly shaped ovals, showcasing a crispy, textured exterior. Hints of rustic red tomato flecks and soft white rice are visible within the fritters. A small sprig of fresh green parsley is casually placed beside them, adding a touch of color. The plate sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A casually folded, plain linen napkin is nearby, adding to the relaxed atmosphere. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in feel. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 1 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add another 15 ml oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 15-18 minutes.
Remove rice from heat. Fluff with a fork. Stir in cooked chicken. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let mixture cool completely.
Beat eggs in a shallow bowl. Place breadcrumbs in another shallow bowl.
Form rice and chicken mixture into small, oval-shaped fritters, about 5 cm long.
Dip each fritter in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs, ensuring full coating.
Heat remaining 500 ml vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C (350°F).
Carefully place fritters into hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding. Fry until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Turkey Ricotta Meatballs with Sugo
recipes.visual_description: A single white porcelain dinner plate holds a generous portion of Spicy Turkey Ricotta Meatballs with Sugo. Three to four plump, golden-brown turkey meatballs, about 4cm in diameter, are nestled in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce. The sauce, rich with diced tomatoes and softened green peas, pools around the meatballs. A dollop of creamy white ricotta cheese rests atop one meatball, slowly melting into the warm sauce. A scattering of bright green chopped parsley and fresh basil leaves provides a fresh counterpoint, alongside finely grated Parmesan cheese. The presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sugo.
Offer a side of simple green salad with vinaigrette.
Provide extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Prepare Meatballs: In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, 100g ricotta, 50g grated Parmesan, breadcrumbs, egg, 2 minced garlic cloves, dried oregano, 10g chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form Meatballs: Roll mixture into 16-20 meatballs, about 4cm in diameter.

Brown Meatballs: Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add meatballs in batches. Brown meatballs on all sides until golden, about 5-7 minutes. Remove browned meatballs and set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Simmer Sauce: Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add chili flakes and hot sauce. Stir well. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Cook Meatballs: Carefully return browned meatballs to the simmering sauce. Cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until meatballs are cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F).
Add Peas: Stir in green peas. Cook for another 5 minutes, uncovered, until peas are tender and sauce thickens slightly.
Serve: Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot with a dollop of remaining ricotta, a sprinkle of fresh Parmesan, and remaining chopped parsley and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure meatballs are fully cooked to 75°C (167°F).
Adjust chili flakes and hot sauce to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Tomato Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A golden-crusted, baked chicken breast, presented whole, rests prominently on a bed of savory, reddish-brown tomato-infused brown rice. The rice is moist, showcasing bits of finely diced onion and vibrant crushed tomato. Around the chicken and rice, roasted carrot chunks, approximately 2cm, display a slight caramelization, adding a pop of orange and tender texture. Melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese, with golden-brown spots, drapes invitingly over the chicken and rice. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The dish is served as a single, refined portion on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. Silver flatware is neatly placed beside the plate, alongside a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's comforting appeal in a casual bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in brown rice, crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken breasts to the skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Cut carrots into 2cm chunks or thick wedges. Arrange carrot chunks around the chicken in the skillet.
Cover skillet tightly with a lid or foil. Bake 30 minutes.
Remove cover. Sprinkle mozzarella cheese over the chicken and rice.
Bake uncovered 10-15 minutes more, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Root Vegetable & Lavender Comfort Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Root Vegetable & Lavender Comfort Soup is presented in a deep, textured ceramic bowl. The soup is hearty, showcasing visible chunks of tender diced potatoes and carrots within a creamy, off-white broth. A subtle swirl of rich sour cream is visible on the surface, partially blending into the soup. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled unevenly over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in kitchen environment. A casually folded cloth napkin is placed beside the bowl. The lighting is soft and warm, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the soup's comforting texture. The overall presentation is simple, unpretentious, and inviting, emphasizing wholesome home cooking.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced carrots and potatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in vegetable broth. Add dried lavender. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
In a small bowl, whisk kudzu starch with cold water until smooth. This is your slurry.
Stir the kudzu slurry into the simmering soup. Cook, stirring constantly, until the soup thickens, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove the pot from heat. Stir in coconut vinegar and verjus.
Gently stir in sour cream until fully incorporated. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Broccoli Macaroni Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Broccoli Macaroni Gratin is presented in a small, oval white ceramic gratin dish, placed centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin boasts a rich, golden-brown, bubbly crust of baked Parmesan cheese and macaroni, with hints of creamy white sauce and vibrant green broccoli florets peeking through. Generous 2-3 cm cubes of pan-seared chicken are visible, nestled among the al dente elbow macaroni and bright green broccoli florets. The textures are a contrast of crispy baked top and a luscious, creamy interior. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded grey cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting glow. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp green salad tossed with a simple vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the creamy sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Cook macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente, according to package directions. Drain well.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Immediately plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
In the same pan used for chicken, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion; sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in 100g grated Parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.
Combine cooked macaroni, seared chicken, and blanched broccoli with the cheese sauce in the pan or a large mixing bowl.
Transfer the mixture to a large gratin dish or individual gratin dishes. Top generously with additional grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the top is golden brown.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Pork with Potatoes, Orange, and Bay

selected_ingredients.name: pork
selected_ingredients.comment: Prepackaged pork shoulder with orange peel and bay

recipes.special_requests: Prepackaged pork shoulder with orange peel and bay leaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-roasted pork shoulder is centrally placed on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate. The pork is cut into thick, rustic chunks, showing its tender, fall-apart texture and rich, browned exterior. Several golden-brown roasted potato wedges are casually arranged around the pork. Thin, caramelized orange slices are nestled among the pork and potatoes, adding a subtle burst of color. A small amount of the savory pan juices pools at the bottom of the plate, glistening under warm, cozy kitchen lighting. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard metal fork and knife. The background is minimally cluttered, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, highlighting the comforting, home-cooked appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.

ingredients.name: Prepackaged pork shoulder with orange peel and bay

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat pork shoulder dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork shoulder on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork from the pot.
Cut potatoes into rustic wedges. Slice the onion into thick pieces. Lightly smash garlic cloves. Slice the orange into rounds.
Add onion slices and garlic cloves to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Return pork to the pot. Arrange potato wedges, fresh orange slices, and fresh bay leaves around the pork.
Pour in chicken broth. The liquid should come about halfway up the pork.
Bring the liquid to a simmer on the stovetop. Cover the pot tightly with a lid.
Transfer the covered pot to the preheated oven. Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender.
For a slightly browned exterior, remove the lid for the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Carefully remove pork and potatoes from the pot. Let pork rest for 10 minutes.
Cut pork into thick chunks. Serve pork chunks and potatoes with the pan juices from the pot.
notes: Cooking time may vary based on pork shoulder thickness; ensure it is fork-tender.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Beef Bulgogi with Sautéed Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, savory Korean Beef Bulgogi dish presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thinly sliced, pan-seared beef, cooked to a rich brown, forms a central mound. Alongside the beef are sautéed cremini mushrooms, translucent sliced onions, and bright red diced tomatoes, all glistening lightly. The vegetables maintain distinct shapes and a tender-crisp texture. The entire dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, adding color and texture contrast. There is appropriate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Traditional Korean metal chopsticks and a long spoon are neatly placed beside the plate. A small, elegant white ceramic bowl filled with fluffy white steamed rice sits to the side, along with a small dish of vibrant red kimchi and a small dish of pale yellow pickled radish (danmuji), completing the authentic Korean dining experience. Natural, even light illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed white rice.
Offer various banchan (side dishes) such as kimchi and pickled radishes.
Provide fresh lettuce leaves and ssamjang (spicy dipping paste) for wrapping the beef.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.quantity: 1 large onion, half thinly sliced for marinade, half thinly sliced for sautéing

instructions: Prepare marinade: Combine soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, mirin, grated pear, minced garlic, grated ginger, and black pepper in a bowl. Mix well.
Marinate beef: Add thinly sliced beef and half of the sliced onion to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

Sauté vegetables: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add remaining sliced onion and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned. Add diced tomatoes. Sauté for another 2-3 minutes. Remove from pan and set aside.

Cook bulgogi: Increase heat to high. Add marinated beef to the hot pan in a single layer. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Combine and serve: Return sautéed vegetables to the pan with the cooked beef. Toss gently to combine.
Plate immediately. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
traditional_techniques: Marinating beef with fruit for tenderizing.
Quick pan-frying or grilling at high heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Garlic Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of the salad is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. Roasted broccoli florets, small diced golden-brown chicken pieces, and pale yellow grated Parmesan cheese are casually tossed together. The ingredients are distributed naturally, with some overlapping, creating a visually appealing mix of vibrant greens, off-white, and pale yellow. The light lemon vinaigrette subtly coats all components, adding a gentle sheen. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, casting soft shadows. A standard fork and knife with simple handles are placed next to the plate, suggesting a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.

Cut chicken breast into small, 1 cm diced pieces. Toss with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Pan-fry in a medium skillet over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cooked through and golden. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 25 ml olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
In a large bowl, combine roasted broccoli, diced chicken, and grated Parmesan cheese.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Shrimp & Noodle Fritters with Chili Dip
recipes.visual_description: A small stack of golden-brown, irregular-shaped fritters on a simple, round ceramic plate. The fritters are naturally piled, some slightly overlapping. A small, rustic ceramic bowl of vibrant red chili dipping sauce sits next to the fritters. Each fritter is roughly 5-6 cm in diameter, golden brown with visible specks of red chili and green onion. The texture is crispy on the outside, slightly chewy inside due to tapioca flour, with small chunks of pinkish shrimp and white rice noodles. A light sprinkle of thinly sliced green onion garnishes the fritters. The plate rests on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple, dark-colored cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. Dark wooden chopsticks rest across the small dipping sauce bowl. Warm, inviting lighting creates a homely kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a sweet and spicy dipping sauce (Nuoc Cham style).
Eaten by hand or with chopsticks.

ingredients.name: Fresh Red Chili, finely minced (for sauce)

instructions: Cook rice vermicelli noodles. Drain well. Rinse with cold water. Roughly chop into 2-3 cm lengths.

In a large bowl, combine chopped shrimp, chopped rice noodles, tapioca flour, egg, minced fresh red chili, minced garlic, the white parts of sliced green onions, 15ml fish sauce, 5g sugar, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Prepare the chili dipping sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together 60ml water, 30g sugar, 30ml rice vinegar, 30ml fish sauce, minced fresh red chili, and minced garlic until sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Heat about 2 cm of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Spoon about 30g of fritter mixture per fritter into the pan. Flatten each spoonful to form a round patty, about 5-6 cm in diameter. Do not overcrowd.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and shrimp is cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove fritters from pan. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain oil.
Serve hot. Garnish with the green parts of the sliced green onions. Serve alongside the chili dipping sauce.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Asian Shrimp Noodle Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh Asian noodle salad presented on a simple, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, sitting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The cooked rice vermicelli noodles are loosely piled, forming a base. Pink, plump, whole shrimp are nestled among the noodles. Bright green julienned cucumber and vibrant orange julienned carrots are scattered throughout, adding color and texture. Thin slices of red chili provide a pop of contrasting color. Fresh green mint and coriander leaves are casually mixed in, with some leaves visible on top. A sprinkle of roughly chopped roasted peanuts adds a rustic crunch. The dish is naturally portioned, filling the plate without overcrowding, showcasing a homely, inviting appeal. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small individual ceramic bowls.
Offer chopsticks as traditional utensils.
A small side dish of extra chili sauce or a lime wedge can be provided for personal adjustment.
instructions: Cook rice noodles according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add shrimp to pan. Cook 2-3 minutes until pink and opaque. Remove from heat.
In a small bowl, whisk lime juice, fish sauce, brown sugar, water, minced garlic, and sesame oil to make dressing.
In a large bowl, combine cooked noodles, cooked shrimp, julienned cucumber, julienned carrot, sliced chili, mint, and coriander.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Divide salad into four starter portions. Garnish with chopped peanuts.
notes: For extra spice, leave some seeds in the chili.
Adjust sweetness and sourness of dressing to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Fermented Tomato & Cheddar Galette
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of a rustic, freeform galette is presented on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate. The galette has a golden-brown, slightly irregular, puffed crust. The exposed filling showcases vibrant red fermented tomato wedges, some softened and some holding their shape, interspersed with bubbling, melted golden-orange grated cheddar cheese. Flecks of green, roughly chopped fresh basil are visible throughout the filling. A small, vibrant green dollop of crispy salad green pesto rests beside the galette, adding a contrasting color and texture. The plate is positioned on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly to the side. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery visible, emphasizing the eco-conscious and sustainable theme.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: Slice tomatoes into 1.5 cm thick wedges. Place in a clean jar with 5g sea salt and thyme sprigs. Press down gently. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours until slightly tangy. Refrigerate until use. (Tomato cores and scraps can be saved for vegetable stock).

Make Galette Dough: Combine flour and 5g sea salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until pea-sized crumbs form. Gradually add ice water, mixing until dough comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Preheat Oven: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Prepare Galette Filling: Drain fermented tomatoes. Gently pat dry. In a bowl, combine drained tomatoes, grated cheddar, roughly chopped basil, 15ml olive oil, and black pepper. Mix gently.

Roll and Assemble Galette: On a lightly floured surface, roll dough into a 30 cm circle. Transfer to prepared baking tray. Spread tomato-cheddar mixture evenly over dough, leaving a 4 cm border. Fold dough border over filling, pleating as needed. Brush dough with beaten egg.
Bake Galette: Bake 30-35 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbly.

Make Crispy Salad Green Pesto: While galette bakes, combine 100g salad greens (including stems), walnuts, grated Parmesan (if using), and garlic clove in a food processor. Pulse until finely chopped. Gradually add 60ml olive oil while blending until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve: Let galette cool slightly. Cut into 4 portions. Serve each portion with a dollop or drizzle of crispy salad green pesto.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Sun-Dried Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous, inviting portion of fresh spinach salad rests on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The vibrant green spinach leaves form a natural base, loosely piled and showing their natural texture. Thinly sliced, deep red sun-dried tomatoes are scattered throughout, providing pops of rich color and a chewy contrast. Golden-brown toasted pine nuts are sprinkled generously over the top, adding a warm, nutty hue and crisp texture. A light, glossy vinaigrette glistens on the leaves and tomatoes, subtly coating each ingredient. The salad is casually arranged, with ingredients naturally overlapping, suggesting a home-prepared meal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, possibly with subtle grain visible. A simple, silver fork rests beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, unpretentious atmosphere. The background is minimally cluttered, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen.
instructions: Toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until golden. Set aside.
Thinly slice drained sun-dried tomatoes. Mince garlic cloves.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine fresh spinach, thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes, and toasted pine nuts.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin lightly crisp, rests on a rustic white ceramic plate. Alongside, a generous serving of tender, golden-brown potato wedges, their exteriors slightly caramelized. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are naturally scattered over the chicken and potatoes, adding vibrant green accents. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits nearby. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The plate is positioned on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded blue and white checkered cloth napkin and simple silver cutlery are placed beside it. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, homely family meal. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking sheet for family-style meals.
Pair with a simple green salad or steamed seasonal vegetables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Mince garlic cloves. Finely chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper to the bowl with potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange potato wedges in a single layer on one half of the prepared baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the other half of the baking sheet alongside the potatoes.
Slice the lemon into thin rounds. Place a few lemon rounds on top of and around the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender and browned. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra crispiness, broil chicken for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallops, Tomato Consommé, Tagliolini
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine white bone china plate holds an artfully composed modern European dish. Four perfectly seared scallops, boasting a golden-brown crust and pearlescent interior, are positioned as the focal point, slightly off-center. Beneath them, a delicate nest of freshly cooked, light yellow tagliolini is meticulously coiled. A small, vibrant pool of crystalline tomato consommé, reflecting a deep ruby hue, is poured around the base of the scallops. Beside this, a subtle, glossy smear of rich, deep amber caramelized onion puree adds a touch of earthy color and refined texture. A few finely snipped chives or a single, precisely placed microgreen provides a contrasting verdant accent. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space emphasizing the precision of each element. The plate rests on a cool grey veined marble surface. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and sophisticated simplicity. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant, minimalist flatware are positioned beside the plate.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes, basil, and garlic. Combine with thyme, salt, and pepper. Blend briefly. Place mixture in a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth over a bowl. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, to allow clear liquid to drip. Do not press. Gently warm consommé before serving.

Prepare Caramelized Onion Puree: Thinly slice onions. In a saucepan, melt 20g butter and 10ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add onions and a pinch of sugar. Cook slowly for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very tender. Add 50ml white wine; deglaze. Transfer onions to a blender. Add remaining 30g butter. Blend until perfectly smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Cook Tagliolini: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fresh tagliolini. Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until al dente. Drain immediately. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent sticking.

Sear Scallops: Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 40ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Place scallops in the hot pan, ensuring they do not touch. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side, until a deep golden-brown crust forms and scallops are cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F). Do not overcrowd the pan; sear in batches if necessary.

Plate the Dish: Place a delicate coil of tagliolini slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange four seared scallops artfully around or on top of the tagliolini. Create a small, elegant smear of caramelized onion puree beside the scallops. Gently pour a small pool of warm tomato consommé around the base of the elements. Garnish with a few finely snipped chives or a single microgreen. Serve immediately.

On a large baking tray, combine carrots, potatoes, and onion wedges. Drizzle with olive oil. Season with 3g salt and 1g black pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast vegetables for 30-35 minutes. Stir halfway through. Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.

Add chicken broth, orange peel strips, and bay leaves to the skillet.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Chicken Bites with Crispy Rice Cakes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, reflecting a natural, minimalist aesthetic. Two golden-brown, pan-fried crispy rice cakes, about 1 cm thick, form the base on one side of the plate. Their surfaces are visibly textured and crisp. Alongside, irregularly cut, succulent chunks of caramelized chicken, approximately 2 cm cubes, are artfully arranged, showcasing their rich, reddish-brown color from the fermented chili marinade. A vibrant, glossy red chili sauce is lightly drizzled over the chicken and rice cakes, creating subtle trails. A scattering of bright green chopped cilantro leaves and thinly sliced scallion rings adds fresh color and natural garnish. The composition is clean and ingredient-focused, with ample white space on the plate. The background features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface and an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, with soft, diffused natural lighting illuminating the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The entire plate is visible, emphasizing a clean, unfussy presentation.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Place in a bowl.
Add 30g fermented red chili paste, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, salt, and pepper to chicken. Mix well. Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Form cooled cooked rice into 8 small, flat cakes, about 1 cm thick. Press firmly.
Heat a non-stick pan with a thin layer of cooking oil over medium-high heat.
Place rice cakes in the hot pan. Cook 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Remove and set aside.
Toss marinated chicken with cornstarch until lightly coated.
Add more cooking oil to the same pan if needed. Increase heat to high.
Add chicken cubes to the hot pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and lightly caramelized, about 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
In a small bowl, mix remaining 30g fermented red chili paste with 15ml hot water to create a thin sauce.
Arrange 2 crispy rice cakes on each plate. Top with cooked chicken chunks.
Drizzle chili sauce over chicken and rice cakes. Garnish with chopped cilantro and sliced scallions. Serve immediately.
notes: Utilize chicken trimmings to render fat for cooking or to make a small, flavorful broth.
Use rice cooking water to nourish houseplants or for composting.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Herb Rice Salad with Chili-Lime Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai-inspired rice salad is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. A mounded, colorful rice salad fills the main portion, featuring fluffy white jasmine rice with crisp diced cucumber, red bell pepper cubes, julienned carrots, and sliced red onion. Fresh green mint, cilantro, and green onions are tossed throughout, adding vibrant color. Small, golden-brown seared chicken breast chunks are neatly arranged beside the salad mound. Roasted peanuts are sprinkled over the salad for textural contrast. The dressing lightly coats all ingredients. The entire plate is visible with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights freshness.

Offer a small dish of dried chili flakes for those desiring extra heat.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, or chopsticks for the chicken.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Cook rice with water in a rice cooker or pot according to package directions. Let cool completely.

For the dressing, finely mince fresh red chilies and garlic. In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, minced chilies, and minced garlic. Stir until sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes. Slice into 1 cm thick pieces or small chunks.
Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Dice red bell pepper into 1 cm cubes. Julienne carrot into thin strips. Thinly slice red onion.
Roughly chop mint leaves, cilantro leaves, and green onions. Roughly chop roasted peanuts.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled rice, diced cucumber, diced red bell pepper, julienned carrot, sliced red onion, chopped mint, chopped cilantro, and chopped green onions.
Pour dressing over the rice and vegetable mixture. Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Divide the rice salad among four serving plates. Arrange sliced chicken pieces beside or on top of each salad portion. Garnish with extra fresh herbs and a few chopped peanuts.

Adjust chili quantity in dressing based on desired spice level.
For added flavor, marinate chicken in a small amount of fish sauce and lime juice before searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Chili Broth with Forbidden Rice

instructions: Combine chicken bones/carcass, vegetable scraps, smashed garlic, sliced ginger, and 2.5 L water in a large pot. Bring to a simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 2-3 hours. Strain broth. Discard solids. Season broth with salt and pepper.
Poach chicken breast/thighs in a separate pot of water until cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken. Shred or dice chicken. Set aside.
Rinse forbidden rice. Cook 200g forbidden rice with 400ml water in a pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Cover. Simmer 25-30 minutes until water is absorbed. Let stand 10 minutes. Fluff rice.

Heat strained chicken broth. Stir in 2-3 tablespoons fermented chili paste. Add 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon rice vinegar. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add shredded chicken. Add 200g seasonal greens; cook until just wilted.

Divide cooked forbidden rice into four individual bowls. Ladle hot soup over rice. Drizzle with 0.5 teaspoon sesame oil over each bowl. Garnish with finely sliced green onion tops and fresh cilantro leaves.

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (e.g., Chianti or Merlot)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered, about 5-7 minutes. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon and set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.

Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Sear chicken thighs in the hot fat until deeply browned on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Work in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften and become translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until fragrant and tomato paste darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is mostly evaporated, about 3 minutes.
Return seared chicken thighs and cooked pancetta to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until chicken is fork-tender and easily shredded. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

Remove chicken from the pot. Discard rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Using two forks, shred the chicken into rustic chunks. Return shredded chicken to the ragu. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente.

Drain pasta, reserving about 125 ml of pasta water. Add the drained pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to reach desired consistency.
Serve immediately in warm bowls, topped with a generous sprinkle of grated Pecorino Romano cheese and a few small basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) during cooking.
The ragu can be made a day in advance; flavors deepen overnight. Reheat gently before combining with pasta.

recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, natural ceramic plate in an earthy tone, set against a light bamboo or reclaimed wood surface. ingredients.name: Hard cheese (e.g., Pecorino, Parmesan) or fresh soft cheese

instructions: Part 1: Lacto-Fermented Tomato Paste (Prepare at least 1 week in advance)
Wash 1 kg ripe tomatoes. Remove stems. Roughly chop.
Blend chopped tomatoes into a coarse puree.
Add 20g sea salt to the puree. Mix well.
Transfer to a clean glass jar, leaving 2-3 cm headspace.
Cover with an airlock lid or a regular lid loosely to allow gas escape.
Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess and effervescence.
Once fermented, transfer to a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth over a bowl. Let drain overnight in the refrigerator to create a thick paste. Reserve liquid (tomato brine) for other uses.
Store the fermented tomato paste in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to several weeks.
Part 2: Chicken & Vegetable Stock (Zero-Waste)
If using bone-in chicken, debone the chicken thighs. Reserve bones.
Collect chicken bones, vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot ends, celery leaves), and any cheese rinds.
Place in a large pot. Cover with 2 litres cold water.
Bring to a simmer. Skim any foam.
Simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours.
Strain the stock. Discard solids. Set aside.
Part 3: Chicken Ragu
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 diced onion, 2 diced carrots, 2 diced celery stalks to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add 4 cloves minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with 100 ml dry red wine (optional, or use a splash of reserved tomato brine or stock), scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in 150g of the prepared fermented tomato paste. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Pour in 500 ml chicken and vegetable stock.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and easily shredded. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred the chicken meat using two forks.
Return shredded chicken to the ragu. Stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered for another 10-15 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Part 4: Fresh Noodles & Assembly
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add fresh noodles. Cook according to package instructions until al dente (usually 2-4 minutes).
Drain noodles, reserving a small amount of pasta water.
Add drained noodles directly to the ragu. Toss to coat, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to reach desired consistency.
Divide noodles and ragu among four serving bowls.
Garnish with freshly grated hard cheese or a dollop of fresh soft cheese.
Sprinkle with fresh basil leaves, roughly torn.

Add chopped onion to pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar. Bring to simmer. Scrape up browned bits.
Return pork to pot. Liquid should cover halfway.

A rich, glossy pan sauce, light brown in color, is naturally pooled around the pork and onions. A few fresh green thyme leaves are casually scattered on top for a hint of freshness. The setting is a homely family kitchen, illuminated by warm, cozy lighting from overhead fixtures, casting soft shadows. A standard, slightly worn metal fork is placed beside the plate. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a lived-in kitchen atmosphere, emphasizing comfort and approachability. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the dish.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Thinly slice both yellow onions.
Heat 15g butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C. Remove pork chops from skillet and set aside on a plate, tented with foil.

Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30g butter to the skillet. Add sliced onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until onions are deeply caramelized and tender. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
Pour chicken broth into the skillet, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return pork chops to the skillet with the sauce and onions. Add fresh thyme sprigs. Spoon sauce and onions over the chops. Simmer for 1-2 minutes to reheat the chops.
Serve immediately with the caramelized onions and pan sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet & Tangy Chicken Bites with Fermented Corn & Mushroom Relish
recipes.visual_description: A clean, minimalist presentation features roasted chicken cubes, golden and slightly caramelized, arranged organically on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Adjacent, a vibrant mound of lacto-fermented corn and thinly sliced pickled mushrooms provides a textural and color contrast, showcasing natural yellows, earthy browns, and the deep green of fresh basil. Scattered crispy rice pieces, irregular in shape and light golden, add a rustic texture. The composition respects negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The plate sits on a light bamboo surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the ingredients' inherent beauty and sustainable origins.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil leaves, finely chopped (for relish)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Corn & Mushroom Relish: Combine corn kernels, sliced mushrooms, sea salt, and apple cider vinegar in a clean jar. Pour filtered water over to cover. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Stir in chopped basil once fermented. Store in refrigerator.

Marinate Chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken cubes with soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, grated ginger, minced garlic, white pepper, and sesame oil. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes. Refrigerate if marinating longer than 30 minutes.

Make Crispy Rice: Preheat oven to 180°C. Spread cooked day-old rice thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Drizzle with neutral oil and sprinkle with salt. Bake for 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and crispy. Let cool completely. Break into small, irregular pieces.

Cook Chicken: Preheat oven to 200°C. Arrange marinated chicken cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway, until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and lightly caramelized.

Assemble Snack: Arrange chicken bites organically on a minimalist ceramic plate. Spoon generous amounts of the fermented corn and mushroom relish alongside. Scatter crispy rice pieces around. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing corn cobs and mushroom stems for future vegetable stock, and day-old rice for crispy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The golden-yellow broth is clear, with visible steam rising. Within the broth are hearty, irregular chunks of cooked chicken, approximately 2cm cubes. Soft, fluffy white rice grains are suspended throughout. Bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and translucent diced onions are interspersed, adding color and texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside it. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen at home.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

instructions: Dice chicken into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Dice carrots, celery, and onion. Add to the same pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Add rice. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Agnolotti del Plin with Braised Short Rib and Parmesan Consommé
recipes.visual_description: Eight to ten perfectly formed, golden agnolotti del plin are artfully arranged in a flowing, organic line on a pristine white bone china rectangular platter. Each delicate pasta parcel, subtly translucent, reveals glimpses of the rich, dark braised short rib filling within. A small, clear amber pool of concentrated Parmesan consommé cradles a few agnolotti, adding a refined sheen. The composition features abundant negative space, highlighting the precision of the pasta and the deep, inviting colors. A few vibrant green micro basil leaves are precisely placed, providing a fresh contrast. The setting is a luxurious grey-veined marble surface with dramatic, focused lighting casting subtle shadows. A crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely, sits nearby. The presentation is ultra-minimalist and elegant, focusing solely on the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a delicate antipasto.
Present on elegant serving platters for communal sharing.
instructions: Pat short ribs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Sear short ribs in olive oil until deeply browned on all sides. Remove ribs.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to pot. Sauté until softened. Add garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Deglaze with red wine. Reduce by half. Return ribs to pot. Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in oven at 160°C (325°F) for 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Remove ribs. Strain braising liquid. Discard solids.
Shred beef, discarding bones and excess fat. Reduce strained braising liquid over medium heat until thickened. Mix shredded beef with reduced liquid. Cool completely.
For pasta dough, combine "00" flour, egg yolks, water, and pinch of salt. Knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes. Wrap in plastic. Rest 30 minutes at room temperature.
For Parmesan consommé, combine Parmesan rind and 500 ml beef stock in a saucepan. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Roll pasta dough very thin (setting 7 on pasta machine). Place small mounds of short rib filling (about 5g each) on one half of pasta sheet, spaced 2 cm apart. Fold pasta over filling. Press around filling to seal. Cut and pinch to form small agnolotti del plin. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Cook agnolotti for 2-3 minutes, until al dente and floating. Do not boil vigorously.
Plate 8-10 agnolotti per serving on a warm platter. Ladle a small pool of warm Parmesan consommé beside or beneath them. Garnish with a few micro basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure short rib filling is completely cooled before making agnolotti to prevent tearing the pasta.
Roll pasta dough as thin as possible for the authentic agnolotti del plin texture.
The Parmesan consommé should be very clear and intensely flavored.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Medallion, Smoked Paprika Potato Puree, Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented on a round, matte white ceramic plate, occupying the lower third. Abundant negative space defines the composition. A creamy, pale orange smoked paprika potato puree is artfully swept across the plate, creating a delicate, organic curve. A perfectly seared, golden-brown chicken medallion, presented as a single, thick, whole piece, rests elegantly beside the puree. Its exterior boasts a subtle crispness. Three to four slow-roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly burst and caramelized, are strategically placed to add vibrant red accents. A few delicate green microgreens are precisely arranged atop the chicken, offering a fresh, contrasting color and texture. The plate sits on a grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed to the side. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the food is the sole focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F).
Wash cherry tomatoes. Place in a small baking dish. Add peeled garlic cloves and 20 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 45 minutes until tender and slightly collapsed. Set aside.
Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2 cm cubes. Place in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 minutes until very tender.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pan over low heat for 1 minute to dry. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a bowl.

Heat milk and butter in a small saucepan until butter melts and milk is hot. Gradually whisk hot milk mixture into riced potatoes until smooth. Stir in smoked paprika. Season with salt and pepper. Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Keep warm.
Pat chicken breast dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Cut each breast into two equal thick medallions.

Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken medallions for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.

To plate, place a dollop of smoked paprika potato puree on one side of each plate. Create a natural, flowing sweep with the back of a spoon. Place one seared chicken medallion next to the puree. Arrange 3-4 slow-roasted cherry tomatoes around the chicken. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hokkaido-Style Miso Salmon with Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hokkaido-Style Miso Salmon is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a simple wooden table. A perfectly pan-seared salmon fillet, golden-brown and flaky, is the focal point, glistening with a rich, savory miso-butter glaze. Around the salmon, a colorful medley of tender, roughly chopped green cabbage, translucent sliced onions, earthy sliced shiitake mushrooms, and vibrant red tomato wedges are artfully arranged, all coated in the glossy, umami-rich sauce. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, thinly sliced green onions and a delicate sprinkle of white sesame seeds, adding fresh contrast and texture. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space, highlighting the fresh ingredients and their cooked textures. A small, pristine white ceramic bowl of fluffy steamed white rice and a pair of traditional wooden chopsticks rest neatly beside the plate, completing the authentic Japanese bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the dish's inviting colors and professional presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed white rice.
Accompany with a small side of pickled ginger (gari) or a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi for extra flavor.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Combine miso paste, sake, mirin, soy sauce, sugar, minced garlic, and grated ginger in a bowl. Whisk until smooth. Set aside.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season lightly with salt on both sides.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or cast iron pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Flip the salmon.
Arrange sliced onions, roughly chopped cabbage, and sliced shiitake mushrooms around the salmon in the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring vegetables occasionally, until they begin to soften.
Pour the prepared miso sauce evenly over the salmon and vegetables. Cover the pan with a lid.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until salmon is cooked through and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add tomato wedges to the pan in the last 2-3 minutes of cooking to warm them through.
Dot the salmon and vegetables with butter chunks. Let the butter melt and coat the dish.
Garnish generously with thinly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of white sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
